draft.title: Chirality in medicines
card: A carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups is called a chiral carbon. If two of the four groups are the same, the carbon is not chiral.
A molecule with a chiral carbon exists as two forms that are mirror images. They cannot be placed on top of each other, like a left hand and a right hand. These forms are called enantiomers.

Enantiomers have the same formula and the same bonds, so many of their physical properties match. They can differ in how they act in the body, because body molecules such as enzymes and receptors are also chiral.
One enantiomer of a medicine may work as intended while its mirror image works less well, does nothing, or causes different effects. This is why a medicine may be made or sold as one pure enantiomer.
draft.remember: Four different groups make a carbon chiral, and its mirror-image forms can act differently in the body.

a.q: Which carbon atom in a molecule is chiral?
opts: One bonded to four different groups
One bonded to two identical groups
One bonded to a double bond to oxygen
One bonded to three hydrogen atoms
a.why: A chiral carbon has four different groups, so its mirror image cannot be placed on top of it. A carbon with two identical groups, such as three hydrogens, has no mirror-image form. A carbon in a double bond has only three groups attached.
a.clue: Count the groups on the carbon and check whether any repeat.

b.q: A drug company in Geelong makes a medicine as a mix of two enantiomers. Only one enantiomer treats the illness. Why might the other enantiomer act differently in the body?
opts: Body molecules such as receptors are chiral too
The two enantiomers have different molecular formulas
The two enantiomers have different bonds between atoms
The other enantiomer has no chiral carbon in it
b.why: Enzymes and receptors in the body are chiral, so each enantiomer fits them differently. The enantiomers have the same formula and the same bonds, so a difference in formula or bonding is not the reason. Both forms come from a chiral carbon.
b.clue: Think about what the body molecules that the medicine meets are like.

a.best: One bonded to four different groups

b.best: Body molecules such as receptors are chiral too

problems.detail: Why (a) says a carbon with two identical groups 'has no mirror-image form'. Every molecule has a mirror image. For an achiral carbon, the mirror image can be placed on top of the original, so it is the same molecule and not a separate enantiomer. It should say the mirror image is identical or superimposable.
